_comment: 📰 XML 1.0/✳️valid's own contribution to the repository test platform: `quick-xml` 0.42 registered as the independent reference reader/writer for THIS subset's own 9-kind `XmlValidMutation` vocabulary, and the comparison profile that vocabulary is measured under. A distinct id and capability from the sibling `✳️any` registration: a mutation vocabulary belongs to the subset that declares it, and reusing an approved oracle outside its surveyed capability fails the contract's oracle-capability-mismatch check.

oracles.rationale: quick-xml is a general streaming XML reader AND writer, not a validating processor: it hands the DOCTYPE back as one raw string and never looks at it again, which is exactly what makes it usable as the independent producer for a VALIDITY vocabulary. This subset's oracle (../🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs) builds its document tree from quick-xml's event stream through the shared 📰markup family module, then decomposes that raw DOCTYPE with its OWN hand-rolled XML 1.0 §2.8/§4.2 grammar, applies each declared XmlValidMutation kind, derives the four §2.8/§2.9 verdicts straight from the W3C text, and re-serializes with quick-xml's Writer. It never imports this repository's own parse_doctype/xml_document_to_text codec, nor its check_valid_conformance. Both encode the same normative rules; neither is derived from the other, which is the point. Registered by this subset rather than shared with ✳️any because the two catalogs have exactly one kind in common (set-text) and disagree about what the DOCTYPE is for.

comparisonProfiles.description: XML 1.0 ✳️valid mutation round trips compared on the ground the subset is defined on: the XML declaration decomposed into version/encoding/standalone, the DOCTYPE decomposed into Name, SYSTEM/PUBLIC external identifier and the ORDERED internal-subset entity declarations (§4.2 binds the first declaration of a name, so order is normative and is never sorted), the document element's name, the four §2.8/§2.9 validity verdicts derived independently by each side, and the element/text/CDATA/comment/PI tree. Attributes are compared as a name-sorted set, because XML attribute order is real writer freedom; sibling and child order IS normative and is never sorted. Self-closing versus explicit empty open/close tags are equivalent by construction — both parse to zero children — and are never distinguished by either side. Nothing about validity is narrowed away: the presence of the DOCTYPE, the agreement of its Name with the document element, and the standalone/external-subset pair are exactly what the comparison sees.
